catalog_quote: 長音を別扱いにしたのは，この方言の（本来の）自立語は必ず重音節を 1 つは含むという制約により，入力形がその条件を満たさない場合は「長音」を挿入するという規則があり，その長音を含む重音節がアクセント型に影響するからである（「最後の重音節」の直後が下降 / 上昇の転換点となるのが基本）。「ハム，マスク，リスト，アクセル」など，短い単語にこれに反するものがいくつか見つかるが，いずれも，より新しく入ったと見られる単語である。 ... （3）音調記号（○は任意の拍） [○：○の直前の上昇（上げ）。 ○]：○の直後の下降（下げ）。 ○]（語末）：○の後の軽音節助詞（主に主格の nu）が下がる。

audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: both the deciding passage (Uwano 2015 sec. 3 p.179) and the supporting register-preservation passage (Uwano 2014 sec. 4 p.143; heavy-syllable definition p.142) are verbatim in the held NINJAL PDFs/text layers at the stated locators. (2) The classification 'tonal' (qv tonal-OR-pitch accent, no stress domain) rests on first-hand accent reports by Uwano, the primary fieldworker on this dialect since 1977; every other source opened — Hayata 1995 ('単語声調方言'), Lawrence 2016 (three lexical tone classes A/B/C, 高起/低起), Lévêque & Pellard 2023 ('word-tone system where melodies are mapped onto whole word forms.. strong interdependence between tone pattern and syllable weight'), and Kato 2022 for the neighbouring Isen dialect ('pitch accent language where H and L are distinguished') — confirms a lexical word-tone/pitch accent system with an obligatory heavy syllable and no stress. G

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: 'In Asama, all phonological words must include at least one heavy, i.e. bimoraic, syllable ... Asama is also characterized by a word-tone system where melodies are mapped onto whole word forms (Uwano 1977, Hayata 1995, Lawrence 2015, Uwano 2016), and there is a strong interdependence between tone pattern and syllable weight ... Inflected forms of verbs show four distinctive tone patterns: H, LH, HL and LHL.' No stress is described.
sources.locator: sec. 1-2, HAL PDF p.2 (the text layer); sec. 5.3.3 'Tone alternations'

sources.citation: Lawrence, Wayne (2016 [cited 2015]) 'Tokunoshima Asama hōgen no meishi onchō ni tsuite nidai: kōki onchō to shishō gokei no onchō' [Two topics on noun tone in the Asama dialect of Tokunoshima], Ryūkyū no Hōgen 40: 1-17, doi:10.15002/00013673
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: Every Asama word form must contain at least one heavy syllable; simple nouns fall into three lexical tone classes A (high from word onset, 2nd-mora syllable heavy), B and C (low-beginning, final mora/syllable high, distinguished by position of the heavy syllable); discusses whether the high-register (高起) class has one or two contrastive patterns. Tone ('音調') throughout; no stress.
sources.locator: sec. 1.1 '単純名詞の音調と音節の軽重' p.1-2

sources.citation: Hayata, Teruhiro (1995) 'Tokunoshima Amagi-chō Matsubara to Asama no hōgen no meishi akusento taikei: tango seichō hōgen no rei to shite' [The noun accent systems of the Matsubara and Asama dialects, Amagi, Tokunoshima: as examples of word-tone dialects], Ryūkyū no Hōgen 18/19: 132-144, doi:10.15002/00012659
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: Reanalyses Uwano 1977's Asama data: Uwano treats it as high-beginning vs low-beginning word-tone (式) plus a pitch-turn locus; Hayata argues the nouns form 'a very simple two-pattern word-tone system' (非常にあっさりした２型単語声調体系). Either analysis is lexical tone/pitch-accent, not stress.
sources.locator: sec. 2 '浅間方言' pp.136-137 and (5) '浅間方言の名詞のアクセント体系'
